name: uri-double-trailing-dot-san-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees uniformResourceIdentifier is '.example.com.'. The leaf's URI SAN is 'foo://bar.example.com../path' — the host ends in two dots, equivalent to an empty trailing label. DNS hostname syntax permits exactly one optional trailing dot (representing the DNS root); a double trailing dot is malformed. A validator that normalises by stripping one trailing dot will compare 'bar.example.com.' against the constraint and incorrectly accept; a strict parser rejects the URI as syntactically ill-formed.
notes: Probes whether a validator distinguishes 'one trailing dot' (legal absolute-DNS-name form, often normalised away) from 'two trailing dots' (illegal empty label). Pre-BoringSSL OpenSSL family does no DNS-syntax validation on the URI host and would attempt a string suffix-match, accepting on coincidence.
